newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Vranitzky in new talks as Albania blast kills four.
newsitem.headline: Vranitzky in new talks as Albania blast kills four.

text.p: Four people were killed and 14 injured in an explosion at an Albanian ammunition dump on Thursday as European envoy Franz Vranitzky held intensive talks to stop the country from sliding back into chaos.

The death toll was confirmed by a spokesman for the multinational force which is protecting aid supplies in Albania. Between 10 and 15 people were still trapped inside the dump near the southern city of Gjirokaster.
Officials spoke of a "big dynamite explosion", but the cause was unclear.
Vranitzky, on his fifth mission to Albania and his second within a week, talked with President Sali Berisha and Prime Minister Bashkim Fino as he tried to get early general elections back on track.
Vranitzky was striving to get parties to agree on rules for the elections, part of international efforts to restore stability to the small Balkan state.

Albania, which spent four and a half decades under Stalinist rule until the early 1990s, descended into violent unrest earlier this year after the collapse of high-yielding pyramid investment schemes. Thousands of people lost their life savings.
Vranitzky's latest mission came as a fresh crisis loomed over the planned elections. Most parties have threatened to boycott them over rules which they say favour Berisha's former ruling Democrats.
Berisha, faced with that threat, on Wednesday postponed a decree to call the elections.
The smaller parties, led by the Socialists, want more seats allocated on a proportional basis, while the Democratic Party favours more decided by majority vote.
The Socialists pulled out of the last elections in May 1996, which international observers said were flawed.
To meet a target date of June 29 for the election, Berisha would, by law, have to issue a decree on Thursday, 45 days before the vote.

Vranitzky, envoy for the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), had a day of tough talks to find a compromise over the election law and get all parties to take part in the planned vote.
He was tight-lipped after his meetings.
"It was a good meeting," he said after talks with Prime Minister Bashkim Fino.
Socialist Party chief Fatos Nano said after talks with the envoy that he hoped for compromise.
"We have to believe that Vranitzky will not fail," Nano told journalists.

In a reminder of the powder-keg situation in the country, shots rang out at one point outside the building where Fino and Vranitzky met. Nervous soldiers fired twice in the air after a car refused to stop at a checkpoint.
Elsewhere, gunmen unleashed a round of bullets in a street of eastern Tirana in what was believed to be a gang fight.
Volleys of gunfire during the night are still common in the capital although shooting during the day has been rare.
